title: Separate-period tests did not resolve a hidden annual temperature response in 217 English river communities
abstract: A small thermal score can miss community change in other directions. We tested this possibility with 3,715 autumn samples from 217 English river sites and 79 family labels. We fitted family temperature-response vectors separately in 2001-2008 and 2009-2017, with chemistry, date and fixed-effect controls. We split their cross-period product into parts along and perpendicular to a spatial temperature vector trained in 1991-2000. The total product was 0.000919 and the perpendicular part was 0.000628 squared Hellinger units per C squared. Their 95% crossed resampling ranges were -0.00386 to 0.00646 and -0.00373 to 0.00630. Thus these records did not establish a repeatable hidden response. We supply a projection test, its error-bias identity, and simulations. Cross-period products remove squared-norm noise bias only under independent zero-mean errors. Shared sites and serial errors can violate this condition. Family records, air temperature, selected sites and fixed baseline axes limit inference. This is a new analysis of an existing river source, not an independent network or a causal test.

display.caption: River response products and 95% crossed resampling ranges, with simulation checks of squared-norm bias. The ranges are conditional on fixed baseline axes. Simulation shared errors create false positive products.
